C-WIN-ROLLBACK-PANIC.IntentSummary: Restore the Windows Help-menu rollback (C-WIN-ROLLBACK-PANIC, wave 2a): mt_rollback_restore currently panics on Windows before the first network response because ReqwestFetch::get (src-tauri/src/m068_rollback.rs:956-973) builds a fresh current-thread tokio runtime and calls Runtime::block_on inside Tauri's async command task, so the renderer's invoke('mt_rollback_restore') never settles. Mechanisms fixed at plan time: (R-1) the synchronous verified-restore core — restore_inner with its Windows branch and the macOS gui_restore_core sibling — is extracted into rollback_restore_core and dispatched through tauri::async_runtime::spawn_blocking (the mt_rollback_prepare precedent at :1958-1962), with app.restart()/app.exit(0) staying on the async side strictly after the join; (R-2) the deadline enters ReqwestFetch's client builder only (reqwest::Client::builder with connect + total timeouts, replacing the deadline-less reqwest::get), the Fetch trait and its injected test seams stay synchronous and network-free, and the menu command bounds the whole operation with tokio::time::timeout around the spawn_blocking join; (R-3) the pending installer is accounted by a root-level pending-rollback.json fact (target version, from version, write timestamp, optional child pid) written before the spawn, reconciled by a three-state table (transition confirmed → finalize and clear, exactly as today; in-window or positively-alive → decline, no second installer; window expired without positive liveness → clear and allow the idempotent retry) — positive-failure-only, pid-reuse-bound; F-008 is cut per the spec (prepare_inner and installSignedUpdate untouched). Execution mode: T-001..T-004 run strictly sequentially in one file (single-writer discipline — same-file write-write ordering is a real constraint), each task gated by the m068 cargo filter suite. All unit evidence rides the host-agnostic injected seams on the reference macOS host; the Windows clean-VM acceptance rides and extends the owner-discharged V-M-068 manual protocol and is not auto-discharged by unit tests. Renderer expectation: no bounded-wait guard is added — after R-1/R-2 every command path settles with a real rejection, so autoUpdates.js:406-433 stays as C-RENDER-REVIEW-FIXES left it (the file remains in ObservedWriteScope, expected diff: none). Adjacent documentation debt (outside ObservedWriteScope, owner-executed like the C-UPDATER-REVIEW-FIXES T-012 pattern): the sibling mark-site faq.md exit table gains the exit-8 event=pending row introduced by T-003.

T-001.Title: Off-async relocation of the restore core with restart/exit ordering pinned (R-1, R-4 mechanism)

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: mt_rollback_restore (src-tauri/src/m068_rollback.rs:1971-2029) no longer executes the verified-restore core on Tauri's async command task: the synchronous core — restore_inner with its Windows branch and the macOS gui_restore_core sibling — moves verbatim into a named blocking function rollback_restore_core(app: &tauri::AppHandle, running: String) -> Result<RestoreMenuEnd, String> with enum RestoreMenuEnd { Relaunch, HandoffExit }; the command body is exactly: resolve the running version, dispatch via tauri::async_runtime::spawn_blocking (the mt_rollback_prepare precedent, :1958-1962), map a join failure to a String rejection, and only after the blocking work joins take the terminal action — macOS app.restart() on RestoreMenuEnd::Relaunch, Windows app.exit(0) handoff on RestoreMenuEnd::HandoffExit, or Err(msg) — so Runtime::block_on (ReqwestFetch::get, :956-973) becomes unreachable from the async command context on every platform; the preferences quiescence anchor survives unchanged by resolving app.state::<PrefsState>() inside the blocking core (PrefsState::replace_from_snapshot behind the store mutex, m005_prefs.rs:256-263) — the State<'_> borrow cannot cross spawn_blocking so the command's State parameter is dropped; AppHandle/State are injected arguments, therefore main.rs:933-936 registration and the renderer's bare invoke('mt_rollback_restore') stay untouched; the Fetch trait keeps its synchronous get(&self, url) -> Result<Vec<u8>, String> shape and every injected test seam (CountingFetch, prefs_write, spawn_installer, stage_write, verify_sig) survives with its meaning unchanged; the CLI path (run_cli_rollback, :1806) already runs on the plain process main thread outside any runtime and is not relocated; every panic/join path returns a real Err(String) so the renderer's localized rollback.restoreFailed* notice (autoUpdates.js:406-433) becomes reachable — never a silently unresolved invoke; a unit test pins the dispatch structure by source scan between unique markers (the V-M-071 no-logging-scan precedent): the mt_rollback_restore body contains the spawn_blocking dispatch and neither restore_inner nor gui_restore_core nor block_on appears in the async body, and the pin fails before the fix (the core runs inline in the command body); existing rollback suites keep their bodies and guards, including the macOS-gated rollback_swap/rollback_gui_restore/rollback_norelaunch modules and the C-ROLLBACK-STORE-BUILD-GUARD cfg alignment; F-008 cut binding respected: prepare_inner and installSignedUpdate untouched, mt_rollback_prepare keeps its own spawn_blocking shape.

T-002.Title: Rollback transport deadline in the client builder plus an overall operation bound (R-2)

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: The rollback transport carries explicit deadlines in the production client builder only, with the Fetch trait unchanged: ReqwestFetch::get builds its request client via reqwest::Client::builder() with .connect_timeout(Duration::from_secs(ROLLBACK_CONNECT_TIMEOUT_SECS)) and .timeout(Duration::from_secs(ROLLBACK_FETCH_DEADLINE_SECS)) — the total covering connect, headers and body — replacing the deadline-less reqwest::get(url) default client (:965), and drives it on the existing current-thread runtime (which now only ever executes on spawn_blocking or CLI main threads); the deadline is a builder setting, not a dependency change (Cargo.toml/Cargo.lock untouched; the reqwest blocking feature is NOT enabled and is not needed), and the Fetch trait signature plus all test fixtures stay network-free; restore_windows_flow's two fetches (:1537 feed, :1562 installer) inherit the deadline through the trait object with zero signature change, and the happy path still performs exactly two GETs on Windows and zero on macOS; the typed failure mapping is unchanged — a timed-out fetch is a fetch error mapping to the exit-4-class (4, "feed fetch: …" / "installer fetch: …") on the CLI and a String error on the menu, so a stalled transfer ends the restore before any mutation (fetch strictly precedes verify/stage/prefs — the order is untouched), the rollback set stays byte-identical, the CLI's lifetime flock dies with the process so a fresh probe is never blocked, and the renderer lands in the localized rollback.restoreFailed* notice; the menu command additionally bounds the whole operation by wrapping the spawn_blocking join in tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_secs(ROLLBACK_RESTORE_DEADLINE_SECS)) (tokio's time feature is already declared, src-tauri/Cargo.toml:61) — on expiry the command returns a String rejection while the bounded per-fetch deadline caps the abandoned blocking thread, so no silent unbounded wait remains on any rollback network path; unit tests drive a non-progressing Fetch fixture end-to-end through restore_windows_flow asserting the (4, …) deadline failure leaves zero writes (prefs closure never called, spawn never called, staging empty, set intact) on both the feed and the installer fetch, and the fetch-count contract stays pinned unchanged; a source-scan unit test pins the builder shape (Client::builder() + .timeout(ROLLBACK_FETCH_DEADLINE_SECS) + .connect_timeout(ROLLBACK_CONNECT_TIMEOUT_SECS) present, reqwest::get( absent) so the deadline provably lives in the transport builder, keeping tests deterministic on the reference macOS host with no Windows host and no network.

T-003.Title: Pending-installer accounting: root fact, three-state reconcile, pid-reuse-bound positive-failure-only retry (R-3)

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Before spawning the verified installer the restore persists a pending-rollback fact and the boot/entry reconciliation accounts for it, with the lifetime instance lock and its semantics untouched: a root-level sibling PENDING_ROLLBACK_FILE ("pending-rollback.json", the restore-outcome.json precedent at :88) carries a strict-on-both-sides PendingRollbackRecord { to_version, from_version, at (unix seconds), installer_pid: Option<u32> } — the read side treats a parse failure as absent (the RestoreOutcomeRecord precedent, :848-878); the spawn seam changes to return the child pid (&dyn Fn(&Path) -> Result<u32, String>) and an accounting wrapper composes the production spawn as: write the fact (installer_pid absent) best-effort BEFORE Command::spawn, spawn, then patch installer_pid = child id best-effort — a failed fact write is a logged BLOCK_ROLLBACK_RESTORE marker and the spawn still proceeds (the restore's primary job never fails on accounting; today's unbridged behavior is the fallback, never worse), and the wrapper is a pure-over-seams function so unit tests pin the write-before-spawn order with a temp root and a canned-pid spawner; evaluate_pending_rollback(root, running, now, pid_alive: &dyn Fn(u32) -> Option<bool>) -> PendingDecision implements the table: (a) transition confirmed — running version equals the live manifest's previous_version — stays finalize_finished_restore's existing compare (:828-843) which additionally clears the fact best-effort after the delete (an injected failing writer proves the clear never blocks or delays the confirmed-success finalize); (b) pending — fact age < PENDING_INSTALLER_WINDOW_SECS (fixed at 7200 s: a passive NSIS run of the ~31 MB installer takes minutes; the generous bound is the false-failed guard), or positively-alive pid past the window — decline without spawning a second installer for the same release; (c) expired — age ≥ window with probe negative or probe unavailable (None, e.g. tasklist failed) — clear the fact and allow the idempotent retry; positive-failure-only: inside the window the probe is never consulted and no absence evidence ever declares failure, and a positively-alive pid past the window is treated as suspected pid reuse and stays declined with a BLOCK marker (retry allowed only on the window bound plus no positive liveness); the gate rides restore_inner directly after clear_restore_outcome (:1415) — the single choke point shared by the CLI re-run and the Windows menu path — via a new Option<&dyn Fn(u32) -> Option<bool>> probe parameter (None skips the gate so every existing restore_inner caller and test keeps its meaning; production passes Some with a cfg(windows) tasklist-based probe returning Option<bool>, probe failure → None); a declined re-run is a new terminal CLI outcome — exit 8 with the machine line event=pending (the token already in M-068's MARK_ROLLBACK dictionary; the factored pending_restore_ending maps it purely, the restore_ok_ending precedent) and the human line naming the pending rollback — and a String rejection surfacing the existing localized notice on the menu path (no new locale keys); reconcile_at_boot_inner (:520-531) runs the evaluate after finalize_finished_restore so the next launch resolves in-window stay, expired clear, and reuse-suspected stay with BLOCK markers — every branch fail-open, nothing wedges boot; unit tests pin: write-before-spawn order, fact-write failure logged non-blocking with the spawn proceeding, the boot branches (transition-clear with failing writer, in-window stay, expired clear with retry armed, alive-past-window reuse-suspected stay, absent-fact no-op), the gate declining with zero fetches/spawns/preferences writes and the set byte-identical, and the expired-fact retry running the normal flow to the unchanged event=pending success outcome — all through injected seams on the reference macOS host, no Windows host required.
